faqs.q: Sec. 6-163. - Applications—Entertainment districts, common consumption areas, and promotional associations.
faqs.a:
(a)
Entertainment district.
City council has the sole authority to approve and create entertainment districts
               within the City of Arvada by resolution. A request for an entertainment district shall
               include the following:
(1)
The proposed name of the entertainment district;
(2)
A detailed area map of the proposed entertainment district including the following:
(i)
The boundaries of the proposed entertainment district outlined in red;
(ii)
The total acreage of the proposed entertainment district; and
(iii)
The name, address, license type, and square footage of each liquor licensed premises,
               excluding temporary modifications, specified in C.R.S. § 44-3-103(15)(c), as amended.
(b)
Timing of applications.
An application for a promotional association and common consumption area may accompany
               a request for an entertainment district or may be submitted after city council's approval
               of an entertainment district. Any application for the certification of a promotional
               association shall be accompanied by an application for the issuance of a common consumption
               area license. Applications for promotional associations and common consumption areas
               shall be made to the city clerk upon forms provided by the city clerk.
(c)
Complete application required.
The city clerk shall not accept any application that is not complete in every detail.
               If an omission or error is discovered by the city clerk, the application shall be
               rejected and returned to the applicant for completion or correction without further
               action by the city clerk. The "acceptance date" shall be the date the city clerk accepts
               an application which is complete in every detail, as determined by the city clerk
               in the city clerk's sole discretion.
(d)
Fees.
Licensing fees, as set in the city's fee schedule, must accompany new and renewal
               applications for the certification of a promotional association and the issuance of
               a common consumption area license. Fees will not be prorated for partial years. Fees
               are not refundable, even if an application is denied.
(e)
Certified promotional association.
(1)
A promotional association must:
(i)
Have a board of directors;
(ii)
Have at least one director from each participating licensed premises attached to the
               common consumption area; and
(iii)
Submit annual reports by January 31 of each year to the city clerk that include:
(a)
A detailed map of the boundaries of the common consumption area;
(b)
The common consumption area's hours of operation;
(c)
A list of attached licensed premises;
(d)
A list of the directors and officers of the promotional association;
(e)
An explanation of the security arrangements within the common consumption area; and
(f)
Any violation of article 3 of the Colorado Liquor Code committed by an attached licensed
               premises.
(2)
An application for promotional association certification shall include the following:
(i)
The name of the promotional association to which the common consumption area license
               would be issued;
(ii)
The name and address of any liquor licensed establishment that would be attached to
               and providing alcoholic beverages for consumption within the common consumption area;
(iii)
The name and address of any non-liquor licensed or non-participating liquor licensed
               establishments whose premises are included in the boundaries of the common consumption
               area license;
(iv)
The name and address of each person that is on the board of directors of the promotional
               association;
(v)
A statement of whether there has been any disciplinary action at any of the attached
               liquor licensed premises within the past five years from the application acceptance
               date; and
(vi)
Any other such information and documents as may reasonably be required by the city
               clerk or the authority.
(f)
Common consumption area license.
An application for a common consumption area license shall include the following:
(1)
A site plan for the common consumption area indicating the attached liquor licensees
               and any businesses whose premises are included within the boundaries of the common
               consumption area, with the boundaries of the proposed common consumption area outlined
               in red;
(2)
The name of the entertainment district in which the common consumption area would
               be located and a map indicating the location of the common consumption area within
               the entertainment district;
(3)
Proof of possession and evidence of permission authorizing alcohol consumption from
               any non-liquor licensed or non-participating liquor licensed premises located within
               the common consumption area;
(4)
Proof of liability insurance carried by the promotional association within the liability
               coverage limits set by the city clerk;
(5)
A description of the proposed days and hours of operation and, for common consumption
               area licenses that will operate on an event basis only, all dates for any event occurring
               within that calendar year;
(6)
Evidence of community support, which may include any additional operational requirements
               that the eligible neighborhood organization deems necessary to protect the health,
               safety, and welfare of the surrounding community;
(7)
A parking and transportation plan;
(8)
A health and sanitation plan;
(9)
A security and admission control plan;
(10)
Any required permits or authorizations including, but not limited to, right-of-way
               permits, zoning permits, and fire and building permits; and
(11)
Any other such information and documents as may reasonably be required by the city
               clerk or the authority.
(
Ord. No. 4804
, § 1, 6-6-2022)
